name: MedEx Inc
old_description: MedEx specializes in the Hospice - Home Health area. Our broad line of products, caring compassionate staff, on-call 24/7 for existing clients and patients enable MedEx to provide 100% satisfaction.
about:
MedEx Home Medical Supply operates from two Indiana locations: its headquarters at 5644 S. Meridian Street in Indianapolis and a second branch at 1307 W. Johnson Street in Marion. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The business distributes durable medical equipment (DME) and provides associated services including delivery, setup, pick-up, and patient instruction. Its product range spans medical beds, specialty mattresses, oxygen and respiratory equipment, lifts, shower chairs, Broda chairs, TENS units, orthopedic supports, diabetic shoes and inserts, and mobility aids such as walkers, canes, crutches, and wheelchairs. MedEx also offers equipment rental for hotels, venues, conventions, and special events. The company emphasizes on-time and stat delivery with flexible scheduling, supported by a professional distribution team and transportation logistics.

MedEx serves assisted living facilities, hospice and home-care agencies, hotels and event venues, and direct-to-consumer customers. It accepts major insurance plans, including Medicaid and Medicare, and maintains certified support specialists available 24/7 for existing clients and patients.

The company states that its ability to deliver and interact personally with patients and families sets it apart from other DME providers, combining product access with hands-on service and round-the-clock support.

name: MedShift
old_description: MedShift software solutions unlock growth for manufacturers, increasing sales, improving operations and expanding B2B marketing and sales capabilities.
about:
MedShift is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. The company develops software platforms designed to accelerate sales, streamline operations, and expand marketing capabilities for manufacturers and healthcare providers.

MedShift’s product suite centers on the Velocity Enterprise platform, which comprises six modules—Unified Commerce, Virtual Payments, Subscription Management, Commission Automation, Shipping, and Digital Inventory—that can be deployed individually or together. The company also offers Velocity Lending, a financing application that delivers real-time pricing, approvals, and contract documentation; Velocity Unified Commerce, an e-commerce platform for sales teams and back-office staff; Pulse IoT, which adds connectivity to field devices for usage tracking and service optimization; and Velocity Marketplaces, a direct-to-consumer retail channel for small to mid-size practices. MedShift reports working with more than 50 manufacturers, distributors, and product partners, deploying over $400 million through its lending app, and serving over 5,500 customers across its business lines.

The company’s customers include medical device manufacturers such as Sientra and aesthetic practice management groups like Aesthetic Management Partners (AMP), as well as distributors and healthcare providers in the aesthetic and medical sectors. Its solutions are tailored for manufacturers seeking to automate manual processes, distributors needing streamlined order management, and practices looking to launch direct-to-consumer e-commerce.

MedShift states that its mission is to empower companies to dream bigger by providing software that connects sales, operations, and marketing functions, reducing lag time in deal approvals and enabling new business models through device connectivity.

about:
MedTech AZ operates from Phoenix, Arizona, where it has served the medical equipment repair market for over 40 years. The company was established to provide mechanical and electrical repair services, parts, and consultation for a range of clinical devices.

Its core work covers autoclave repair across more than 20 makes and models, medical chair servicing including re‑upholstery and cosmetic finishes, and digital X‑ray system maintenance. Beyond those specialties, the shop handles a broad variety of medical tools, offers equipment refurbishing, on‑site and remote support, and runs a sales network for new and refurbished units from manufacturers. It also purchases used equipment for resale or parts.

The customer base spans general practice, pediatrics, radiology, oncology, ophthalmology, podiatry, ENT, gynecology, cosmetic and reconstructive surgery, chiropractic, surgical, dental, veterinary, and tattoo practices. MedTech also works with distributors and manufacturers to source replacement parts and complete systems.

The company emphasizes competitive service rates that are often below industry standards and a willingness to refer clients to other providers when a repair falls outside its expertise.

name: Medical Armor Corporation
old_description: PROVIDES REMARKABLE PROTECTION AGAINST CUTS & CALLUSES ON INDEX FINGERS FROM SUTURING
about:
Medical Armor Corporation operates from Fremont, Nebraska, where it has developed and supplied its signature Kevlar surgical underglove for more than three decades. The company remains privately held, though specific ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The firm manufactures a single-layer underglove made entirely of DuPont Kevlar® that is worn beneath standard latex or nitrile gloves. The device carries FDA 510(k) clearance and is produced domestically. Each glove can be re-sterilized and reused up to five additional times, yielding a total of six uses per unit. The company does not publish facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures.

Primary customers include orthopedic surgeons, podiatric surgeons, pathology labs, paramedics, emergency-room staff, and fire and police personnel. Beyond healthcare, the gloves are used in advanced manufacturing, sheet metal work, automotive repair, glass handling, mortuary and coroner services, and home and garden tasks.

The product was created to eliminate the need for bulky protective pads or Steri-Strips on the index finger during suturing. The company emphasizes that its Kevlar layer provides 26 times the cut resistance of a standard latex glove, requires 1,200 grams of force to cut versus 45 grams for latex, and wicks moisture away from the hand while maintaining tactile sensitivity.

name: Medice Manufacturing
old_description: A leading USA manufacturer of solid billet aluminum valve cover spacers, Medice Manufacturing has never had even a single complaint about leaks using their spacers.
about:
Medice Manufacturing operates from Cochranton, Pennsylvania, where it designs and machines valve cover spacers, engine storage kits, and related performance accessories. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or ownership structure.

The product line centers on solid billet aluminum valve cover spacers—offered in 3/8-, 1/2-, and 1-inch thicknesses—that allow factory valve covers to clear high-lift rocker arms, stud girdles, and shaft-mounted rockers. Complementing those are Stor-Em engine storage kits with CNC-machined plastic block-off plates for carburetors, exhaust ports, fuel pumps, and other openings, plus heavy-duty AN wrenches and 1/8-inch aluminum fuel-pump block-off plates. Every part is programmed, milled, and inspected in-house; the company emphasizes that no production steps are outsourced.

Customers include engine builders, racers, and restoration shops needing reliable sealing for performance valve trains, as well as hobbyists and professionals storing or shipping engines. The spacers are used with factory or aftermarket valve covers on applications ranging from street rods to circle-track engines, while the storage kits serve both long-term preservation and short-term paint-shop masking.

Medice attributes its leak-free record to the use of billet aluminum rather than castings and to a fully CNC-controlled process that holds repeatable dimensions. The founder’s original goal was to eliminate the need for tall valve covers, and the current catalog reflects that focus on direct-fit, American-made components with optional custom branding.

name: Medzah Industries
old_description: Disposable 3-Ply Face Masks: Reliable Everyday Protection For Medical Use
about:
Founded in 2016 by Rafey Zaheer in Glastonbury, Connecticut, Medzah Industries began as a minority-owned small business with a mission to transform healthcare supplies through innovation and eco-friendly practices. The company also operates a site in Dallas, Texas, and a second Connecticut location in South Windsor.

Medzah manufactures sterile disposables, including 3-ply face masks and the Bionex smart dispensing system designed to prevent cross-contamination. It assembles custom medical kits and provides third-party logistics (3PL) and supply chain solutions, drawing on a global sourcing network that spans the United States, China, Malaysia, Pakistan, and Vietnam.

The company serves hospitals, clinics, and home-care providers nationwide. Notable customers include Boston Children’s Hospital, which named Medzah its Supplier of the Month in September 2024, and the Greater New England Minority Supplier Development Council (GNEMSDC), which awarded Medzah its Supplier of the Year honor.

Medzah cites its commitment to sustainability, diversity, and innovation as core differentiators. The firm’s recognition as the 2025 Manufacturer of the Year for Connecticut and New England, along with a Firecracker Award and SBA nominations, underscores its focus on reliable, eco-friendly healthcare solutions.

The company manufactures custom printed circuit boards and metal RF shields, offering full-service support that spans design assistance, manufacturing, and value-added services. It serves customers across North America with a focus on meeting specifications, schedules, and sourcing needs, positioning itself as a partner that develops solutions collaboratively.

Mega Circuits serves a North American customer base in industries that require custom printed circuit boards and RF shielding, though specific sectors are not detailed in available materials. A customer testimonial highlights the company's ability to implement last-minute design changes and deliver boards on time to keep production schedules on track.

The company emphasizes responsive, courteous service and on-time delivery as key differentiators, citing its willingness to accommodate urgent design changes and its track record of keeping customer production lines running. This service-oriented approach has underpinned its operations since 1985.
